This my first impressions on a portable USB powered HD monitor called the GeChic 2501C.

I purchased this monitor on Amazon for 200$. I was looking for a portable monitor that would give portability on my PS4 and also add screen estate on my laptop. The 2501C stood out because of its ability to plug and play right out the box. Most other monitors require display drivers which was a feature I was trying to avoid. The thinness and weight of the monitor has surpassed my expectations and its ability to be powered by a standard micro-USB was a plus! While the manufacturers state its max resolution is "1366 x 768", I've gotten it to achieve full 1080p.

TLDR; PROS: Powered by micro-USB, HDMI/VGA output, extremely lightweight for a folding, portable monitor. I think this is a great companion for any laptop needing additional screen estate. CONS: Plastic screen stand feels quite flimsy, but it will get the job done. It does what it was meant to excel in: Portability and lightweight!

Why isn't the downvote button a disagree button?

Because downvoating moves whatever it is down, making it less visible. This silences them to an extent. While nobody is stopping you from downvoating whatever you like, just know that if you downvoat something simply because you disagree, you're promoting a central hivemind.
That makes a lot of sense. I guess if you disagree with something it's better to comment anyway so that people could understand why.
Absolutely. Comment and upvoat, for the sake of the discussion.

Because if you use the downvoat as a disagree button like on that other website, then you get the ultra circlejerk mentality.

In an ideal world, two people on opposites sides of a debate would both get upvoted so that their debate was fully visible. currently, the popular trend is to downvote the person you disagree with, until one of the two individuals "loses" due to a number of downvotes.

its pathetic, and doesn't belong on this website.

People will use it as one, even though it's meant to discourage content or statements that don't contribute to Voat. I think if you disagree with someone you should say why instead of just saying "durrrr me no like, downvoat!".

"durrrr me no like, downvoat!"

Sadly, there seem to be quite a few who do just that.

I think it's a habit that's crossed over from the other place. I don't like using the downvoat button too much either. I think it should be solemnly reserved for spam and shitposts. Mind you there are a lot of circlejerky type hijack comments becoming very popular here too like "I gets the reference" etc. that just makes my virtual blood boil so I'm being compelled more and more to downvoat.
I think you're right. For the most part I try to refrain from downvoating just because I disagree. However, I will admit, I've been compelled to do so a few times.

The idea is that the up/down voting is for judging how a post or comment contributes to discussion. If I disagree with a comment, but it contains well-written, valid discussion, it is worthy of an upvote regardless of my opinions. Using downvotes to signify disagreement eventually creates a hive-minded echo chamber.
Downvoats control content. If you downvoat for things you disagree with, it turns the community into an echochamber because dissenting views are not visible.
That's a solid point. Circlejerks are only fun in person.
I down vote when a post just doesn't make sense or a comment is an off topic rant or a troll comment.
